executive-insights-monthly.statement: The Executive Insights Report provides an organization's key contacts with a monthly overview of the traffic volume and security posture of their organization.

quotes: The Executive Insights Report provides an organization’s key contacts with a monthly overview of the traffic volume and security posture of their organization.

executive-insights-two-sets.statement: There are two sets of recipients: the first receives the report on the first weekend, when it is generated, and the second 7 days after the first. To add a recipient, contact the Zscaler Account team and name the set.

quotes: There are two sets of recipients that receive the report. The first set receive the report on the first weekend, when the report is generated. The second set receive the report 7 days after the first set receive it.
If you want to add a recipient to receive the report, contact your Zscaler Account team to add them. Specify which recipient set you want them to be added to.

executive-insights-widgets.statement: Its widgets include a 6-month overall traffic trend, a Transactions Blocked Average Comparison of three averages, including a peer average and a cloud average, the top 5 locations by bandwidth, a 6-month trend of threats blocked and policy violations, and the top Microsoft 365 apps in the last month.

quotes: Overall Traffic: Trend that displays traffic volume for the last 6 months.
Transactions Blocked Average Comparison: Displays three averages.
Peer average: Displays the average of the percentage of transactions blocked for your peer group
Cloud average: Displays the average of the percentage of transactions blocked for the cloud
Top Locations by Bandwidth: Displays the top 5 locations by bandwidth usage and the bandwidth usage per location.
Threats Blocked and Policy Violations: Displays trend of threats blocked and policy violations for the last 6 months for your organization.
Top Office 365 Application Usage: Displays the top Microsoft 365 apps for your organization in the last month and the bandwidth used per app.

cio-report.statement: The Company Summary Report for Chief Information Officers (CIO Report) is an interactive report whose sections include Peak Transactions, Top Blocked URL Categories and Mobile Traffic by Device Type. The page says a chart can open its logs with View Logs or open in Web Insights with Analyze Chart, and the report can be given notes, favorited, copied, scheduled and printed.

quotes: The Company Summary Report for Chief Information Officers (CIO Report) is an interactive report
- Peak Transactions
- Top Blocked URL Categories
- Mobile Traffic by Device Type
Click View Logs to see its associated logs.
Click Analyze Chart to see the chart in Web Insights and to drill down to the logs.
Add custom notes to the report
Add it your list of favorite reports
Copy the report
Schedule regular email deliveries of the report
Print the report

cso-report.statement: The Company Summary Report for Chief Security Officers (CSO Report) is an interactive report whose sections include Overall Threat Posture, Top Blocked Threat Super Categories for Road Warriors, DLP Engine Violations, DLP Dictionary Violations, Top Categories for Liability Exposure Allowed, Bandwidth Loss Trend and Top Users Infected by Threats.

quotes: The Company Summary Report for Chief Security Officers (CSO Report) is an interactive report
- Overall Threat Posture
- Top Blocked Threat Super Categories for Road Warriors
- DLP Engine Violations
- DLP Dictionary Violations
- Top Categories for Liability Exposure Allowed
- Bandwidth Loss Trend
- Top Users Infected by Threats

cipa-report.statement: The CIPA Compliance Report provides information on the top URL categories blocked from the Legal Liability class, and the top users and domains blocked from accessing obscene or harmful material. To display it within Interactive Reports, CIPA Compliance must be enabled within Advanced Policy Settings.

quotes: provides information on the top URL categories that are blocked from the Legal Liability class, and the top users and domains blocked from accessing obscene or harmful material.
To display the CIPA Compliance Report within Interactive Reports, you must have CIPA Compliance enabled within Advanced Policy Settings.

cipa-7-days.statement: The CIPA Compliance Report cannot be copied and shows data only for the last 7 days, so the Monthly option is grayed out when scheduling it.

quotes: This report cannot be copied. You are only able to see data for this report up to the last 7 days, so when scheduling the report, the Monthly option is grayed out.

cipa-widgets.statement: Its widgets include Top URL Categories Blocked from Legal Liability, top blocked users per category (for example Adult Materials and Newly Registered and Observed Domains) and Top Domains Blocked.

quotes: - Top URL Categories Blocked from Legal Liability
- Top Users Blocked from Adult Materials
- Top Users Blocked from Newly Registered and Observed Domains
- Top Domains Blocked

peer-comparison.statement: The Industry Peer Comparison Report compares the organization's performance and effectiveness for the preceding month to that of peer organizations and all companies using the cloud service. Peers are chosen based on business vertical, geographic region and business size, and accessing the feature gives Zscaler the right to make the comparison.

quotes: compares your organization's performance and effectiveness for the preceding month to that of both peer organizations and all companies using the cloud service.
By accessing Industry Peer Comparison features, you provide Zscaler the right to compare your organization's performance
Peers are chosen based on business vertical, geographic region, and business size.

qbr-generation.statement: A new QBR is generated on the first weekend of every month, or on the following weekend if the first weekend falls on the first or second day of the month. QBRs are stored as PowerPoint files in the Zscaler cloud, up to 15 reports.

quotes: A new QBR is generated on the first weekend of every month. However, if the first weekend falls on the first or second day of the month, then the QBR is generated on the following weekend.
The QBRs are securely stored as a PowerPoint file in the Zscaler cloud. Up to 15 reports are stored.

qbr-enable.statement: A QBR that is not visible is enabled through the support team or a Zscaler Support ticket, and including or excluding remote user traffic goes through the Zscaler Account team.

quotes: If you don't see the QBR, contact your support team or open a Zscaler Support ticket to have it enabled.
If you want to include or exclude remote user traffic, contact your Zscaler Account team.

qbr-peers.statement: The QBR's growth section covers transaction count, bandwidth per user, threats stopped and policy blocks for the current, previous and last year's same quarter, and peers are defined by analyzing industry, geography and company size.

quotes: The growth in your organization's transaction count, bandwidth per user, threats stopped, and policy blocks for the current, previous, and last year's same quarter.
Peers are defined by analyzing your industry, geography, and company size.

qbr-qualified-ssl.statement: In the QBR's SSL/TLS section, qualified SSL/TLS refers to SSL/TLS traffic that excludes UCaaS traffic and, when O365 is enabled, O365 traffic.

quotes: The qualified SSL/TLS in this section refers to the SSL/TLS traffic that excludes UCaaS traffic and O365 (when O365 is enabled) traffic

qbr-sections.statement: QBR sections include a 12-month internet-bound traffic growth graph, Protection Against Advanced Threats, Threats and Locations by Botnet Callbacks, real blocked phishing examples, Office 365 Growth, a Standard or Advanced Sandbox section, and Zscaler Support incidents by priority over the last 90 days.

quotes: The growth graph of your internet-bound traffic on a monthly basis for the last 12 months.
- Protection Against Advanced Threats
- Threats and Locations by Botnet Callbacks
The real examples of phishing attempts on your users that were blocked by Zscaler.
- Office 365 Growth
- Standard or Advanced Sandbox
Zscaler Support Incidents - The number of incidents and their breakdown by priority over the last 90 days and their user impact.

qbr-sandbox-terms.statement: In the QBR Sandbox section, Files required Sandbox is the total number of files sent to the Sandbox for analysis (known files with a unique MD5 and a verdict, or unknown files submitted for offline analysis), and Files unique to your org is the total number of files the organization submitted for offline analysis.

quotes: Files required Sandbox: The total number of files that were sent to the Sandbox for analysis. They were either known files with a unique MD5 and a verdict associated with it, or unknown files that were submitted to the Sandbox for offline analysis.
Files unique to your org: The total number of files submitted by your organization to the sandbox for offline analysis

executive-recipient-sets.title: Who is in each Executive Insights recipient set
executive-recipient-sets.detail: The page says there are two recipient sets and that the Account team adds recipients to a named set. It does not say who is in each set or how sets are assigned.

qbr-period.title: What period a QBR covers, and which roles can download it
qbr-period.detail: A QBR is generated monthly, with up to 15 stored, but the captured page does not say what period each report covers, whether the 15 are the last 15 months, or which roles can download QBRs.

zia-zdx-qbr.title: Whether the ZIA QBR and the ZDX QBR are one report
zia-zdx-qbr.detail: The ZIA QBR page lists threat sections, which bears on the QBR threats question in the ZDX console subject, but no source says the two QBRs are the same report, so their facts are not merged.

report-time-frames.title: Time frames of the CIO and CSO reports and contents of the Peer Comparison report
report-time-frames.detail: The CIO and CSO pages do not state a time frame, and the Industry Peer Comparison page describes no report contents beyond the comparison it makes.
